key_insight: Additively manufactured porous lattice walls can raise hydrogen flashback limits, with the coarsest wall structure giving the strongest improvement by cooling the near-wall mixture.
engineering_relevance: Porous nozzle walls made by metal additive manufacturing offer a practical design lever for safer hydrogen combustors without 크게 altering the overall flow field.
method: 5 combustor nozzle configurations with solid and body-centered cubic lattice walls
Atmospheric hydrogen jet-flame tests across equivalence ratio and Reynolds number 9,000–12,000
Flow-field measurements, flame imaging, and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition to track transition to flashback
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the coarsest porous wall significantly improved flashback resistance while flow and flame shapes changed only slightly across configurations.
watch_item: The mitigation mechanism appears tied to porous-wall cooling and may depend strongly on lattice geometry, operating point, and manufacturable pore quality.
paper_title: Effect of Additively Manufactured Wall Lattice Structures on Flashback Limits in a Hydrogen Jet Flame Combustor
